task_1.title: Add support for newer GCC patch versions
task_1.description: Conan 2.17.0 expands its built-in GCC compiler version support so users can target newer GCC patch releases in standard settings and profiles without version validation failures.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan accepts newer GCC patch releases as valid `compiler.version` values when `compiler=gcc`, so users can configure supported GCC toolchains without rejection.

expectation.grounded: The built-in valid values for `compiler.version` under `compiler=gcc` must include `13.4` and `14.3`. Any Conan workflow that consumes or validates standard settings and profiles should accept those values the same way it accepts previously supported GCC versions.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to declare the newly supported GCC releases in normal Conan configuration and have those compiler versions recognized as supported rather than treated as unknown values.

constraints.grounded: Existing GCC version values that were already accepted must remain valid. The change should only expand the accepted `compiler.version` set for GCC and must not alter the behavior of other GCC settings fields or other compiler families.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should broaden compatibility for newer GCC releases without changing existing compiler configuration behavior outside of recognizing the new versions.

behavior: When `compiler=gcc`, `compiler.version=13.4` is recognized as a valid built-in setting value.
When `compiler=gcc`, `compiler.version=14.3` is recognized as a valid built-in setting value.
Conan setting validation for profiles or explicit settings no longer rejects GCC 13.4 or GCC 14.3 as unsupported built-in compiler versions.
Previously supported GCC compiler versions continue to be accepted unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When a user configures Conan with `compiler=gcc` and `compiler.version=13.4`, it should be accepted as a valid compiler setting.
When a user configures Conan with `compiler=gcc` and `compiler.version=14.3`, it should be accepted as a valid compiler setting.
When Conan validates settings that use older already supported GCC versions, those configurations should continue to behave as before.
When a user uses a non-GCC compiler configuration, this upgrade should not change its accepted version values or validation behavior.

task_3.title: Honor conanws directory as workspace search boundary
task_3.description: Workspace discovery now treats a directory named `conanws` as the upper boundary for locating a Conan workspace and resolves that directory as the workspace root when it contains a supported workspace definition file.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan workspace discovery respects a directory named `conanws` as the top search boundary and resolves the workspace from that directory when it contains a valid `conanws.py` or `conanws.yml` definition.

expectation.grounded: When Conan locates a workspace, it should recognize a directory named `conanws` as a special boundary in the upward search. If that directory contains `conanws.py` or `conanws.yml`, workspace-related operations such as resolving the workspace root should use that directory as the workspace root. If the search reaches a `conanws` directory without either supported workspace file, Conan should treat the workspace as not defined instead of resolving a higher ancestor workspace.
expectation.conceptual: Workspace lookup should stop at a `conanws` directory. That directory becomes the workspace root only when it contains a supported workspace definition file; otherwise the lookup should fail as no workspace being defined rather than silently using one from above.

constraints.grounded: The change must preserve support for both `conanws.py` and `conanws.yml` as valid workspace descriptors, continue to resolve workspaces from the current directory or ancestor directories when no `conanws` boundary is involved, and avoid selecting a parent workspace located above a `conanws` directory.
constraints.conceptual: Existing workspace discovery should keep working for normal directory layouts, but a `conanws` folder must act as a hard boundary and must not allow fallback to a workspace outside that boundary.

behavior: Workspace discovery now gives special meaning to an ancestor directory whose name is `conanws`.
If the current directory is at or below a `conanws` directory and that directory contains `conanws.py`, Conan should resolve that directory as the workspace root.
If the current directory is at or below a `conanws` directory and that directory contains `conanws.yml`, Conan should resolve that directory as the workspace root.

If a `conanws` directory is encountered without either supported workspace definition file, Conan should report that no workspace is defined instead of continuing upward to a higher ancestor workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Given a working directory inside a `conanws` directory that contains `conanws.py`, when Conan resolves the workspace, then it should use that `conanws` directory as the workspace root.
Given a working directory inside a `conanws` directory that contains `conanws.yml`, when Conan resolves the workspace, then it should use that `conanws` directory as the workspace root.
Given a working directory inside a `conanws` directory that does not contain `conanws.py` or `conanws.yml`, when Conan resolves the workspace, then it should indicate that no workspace is defined.

Given a working directory in a normal directory hierarchy without a `conanws` boundary, when Conan resolves the workspace, then existing ancestor-based lookup for `conanws.py` or `conanws.yml` should continue to work.

task_2.title: Rename workspace editables to packages
task_2.description: Conan 2.17.0 renames workspace-managed local entries from `editables` to `packages` across workspace definitions, workspace inspection output, and custom workspace hooks, so integrations must adopt the new term while preserving existing package path and output-folder behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that workspace-managed local packages are defined, discovered, and reported using `packages` instead of `editables`, so existing workspace flows continue to work after upgrading to Conan 2.17.0.

expectation.grounded: Workspace data and public workspace-facing behaviors should use the `packages` name consistently: workspace manifests and generated workspace templates should store package entries under `packages`; `workspace info` should expose a `packages` field; and custom `Workspace` integrations should provide package mappings via `packages()` so path lookup, add/remove persistence, and local package resolution continue to operate from the renamed field. Removal of an unknown workspace package path should still fail with a `ConanException`.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, users should interact with workspaces in terms of packages, not editables. Any workflow that defines local workspace packages, inspects workspace contents, or derives package references from a custom workspace should continue to work with the new naming and preserve the same observable package resolution behavior.

constraints.grounded: The rename must not change the meaning of each workspace entry's `path`, optional `output_folder`, or product membership. Workspace operations that consume these entries should continue to resolve local package references from the stored mapping, and invalid removal requests must remain explicit failures rather than being ignored.
constraints.conceptual: This change should update terminology without weakening existing workspace behavior. Local package entries should still behave the same way, and erroneous package removals should still surface as errors.

behavior: Workspace configuration uses `packages` as the persisted collection of workspace-managed local package references instead of `editables`.
Workspace inspection returns `packages` as the public field that lists mapped local packages and their metadata.
Custom workspace implementations are expected to supply local package mappings through `packages()`, and those mappings drive workspace package discovery and resolution.
Adding or removing a workspace-managed local package persists the change in the `packages` mapping while retaining each entry's path metadata and any optional output-folder or product association.
Removing a path that is not registered as a workspace-managed local package continues to raise a `ConanException` instead of silently succeeding.
acceptance_criteria: When a workspace manifest defines local entries under `packages`, workspace commands that inspect or consume workspace-managed local packages should recognize those entries.
When workspace information is requested, the reported mapping of local workspace packages should be available under `packages` and no longer under `editables`.

When a custom `Workspace` implementation derives local package references dynamically, implementing `packages()` should make those references visible to workspace introspection and package resolution flows.

When a workspace-managed local package is added or removed, the persisted workspace metadata should be updated in the `packages` collection without changing the meaning of its stored path or optional output-folder data.
When removal is requested for a path that is not part of the workspace package mapping, the operation should fail with a `ConanException`.

task_6.title: Support extra configure arguments in GNU toolchains
task_6.description: Conan 2.17.0 adds a GNU toolchain configuration option that lets consumers append extra arguments to the generated `configure` command in `AutotoolsToolchain` and `GnuToolchain`. This allows project-specific `configure` switches to be supplied through configuration while preserving the toolchain's standard shared, install, and triplet-related arguments.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can provide additional GNU `configure` command arguments through Conan configuration when using Autotools-based toolchains.

expectation.grounded: Expose a built-in Conan conf named `tools.gnu:extra_configure_args` for `AutotoolsToolchain` and `GnuToolchain`. When this conf is provided as a list, its entries must be merged into the generated `configure_args` together with the existing default shared-library, installation, and build/host triplet arguments.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to extend the generated `configure` command with extra flags through configuration instead of replacing the toolchain's standard arguments.

constraints.grounded: If `tools.gnu:extra_configure_args` is unset, GNU toolchain behavior must remain unchanged. The extra arguments must be additive, must apply only to `configure` argument generation, and must not affect unrelated generated argument groups such as `make` or `autoreconf`. The conf value is expected to be list-typed.
constraints.conceptual: Leaving the option unset should preserve current behavior. Any added flags should only influence the `configure` step and should be supplied in the expected structured format.

behavior: `AutotoolsToolchain` includes configured extra entries in its generated `configure_args`.
`GnuToolchain` includes configured extra entries in the `configure_args` it uses to render the `configure` command.
The additional entries are combined with existing default shared, install, and triplet-related `configure` arguments rather than replacing them.
Extra `configure` arguments do not propagate to other generated argument sets outside the `configure` phase.
acceptance_criteria: When `tools.gnu:extra_configure_args` is not set, generated GNU toolchain `configure` arguments should remain consistent with existing default behavior.

When a user defines `tools.gnu:extra_configure_args` as a list of `configure` switches, `AutotoolsToolchain` should generate a `configure` command that includes those switches in addition to the standard ones.

When a user defines `tools.gnu:extra_configure_args` as a list of `configure` switches, `GnuToolchain` should generate a `configure` command that includes those switches in addition to the standard ones.
When extra `configure` arguments are configured, they should affect only the `configure` phase and should not appear in unrelated generated arguments such as `make` or `autoreconf` inputs.

task_4.title: Remove workspace home overrides
task_4.description: Conan 2.17.0 removes workspace-level control of the Conan home/cache folder and shifts workspaces toward a package-oriented model with explicit workspace naming, relative package references, and built-in cleanup of package output folders.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Conan 2.17.0 no longer relies on `conanws.yml` or `conanws.py` to select the Conan home/cache folder, and that workspace behavior follows the 2.17.0 package model for naming, persisted package entries, relative paths, and cleanup.

expectation.grounded: Workspace definitions in `conanws.yml` or `conanws.py` must no longer provide a `home_folder` override, and `ConanAPI` cache/home selection must depend only on the explicit `cache_folder` argument or the standard Conan home resolution. Workspace naming should use a declared `name` when present and otherwise fall back to the workspace folder name. Workspace package entries should be persisted and read through `packages` rather than `editables`, package paths should be normalized relative to the workspace folder even when they resolve outside that folder, and the default workspace clean behavior should remove each package `output_folder` while reporting missing output folders or removal failures through normal workspace output.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, a workspace should describe packages and products, not redefine where Conan stores its cache. Workspaces may expose a user-defined display name, continue to reference package locations relative to the workspace even when those locations live outside the workspace directory, and support a standard cleanup operation that removes generated output directories for packages that declare them while reporting non-fatal cleanup issues.

constraints.grounded: Do not preserve any runtime path in which workspace `home_folder` data changes the active Conan cache folder. Preserve folder-name fallback when no explicit workspace name is supplied. Cleanup must stay limited to declared package `output_folder` values, and package path normalization must remain relative to the workspace folder without requiring package locations to stay under the workspace root.
constraints.conceptual: Do not let workspace metadata silently override global Conan home selection, reject valid workspace packages only because they are located outside the workspace directory, or delete directories that are not declared as package output folders. If no workspace name is configured, the previous folder-based default should continue to apply.

behavior: Workspace-defined `home_folder` settings no longer affect the active Conan cache/home directory.
A declared workspace `name` becomes the workspace identity used by workspace-facing behavior; otherwise the workspace directory name remains the default.
Workspace package records are read from and written to `packages` instead of `editables`.
Workspace package paths are stored relative to the workspace folder and may legally point outside the workspace root.

The default workspace clean behavior removes each package `output_folder`, reports packages without an `output_folder`, and surfaces removal failures as warnings rather than treating them as hard failures.
acceptance_criteria: When a workspace definition contains `home_folder` data, using that workspace should not change the Conan home/cache folder selected by the API or CLI.
When a caller provides `cache_folder` explicitly, loading or using a workspace should leave that cache/home folder unchanged.
When a workspace definition includes `name`, workspace identity and output should use that name; when `name` is absent, they should fall back to the workspace directory name.

When workspace packages are added or removed, the persisted workspace model should reflect them under `packages`, and relative package locations should remain valid even when they traverse outside the workspace root.

When workspace clean runs on packages with and without `output_folder` values, it should delete only the declared output folders, continue past packages that do not define one, and report cleanup failures as warnings.

task_5.title: Allow workspace packages outside the workspace folder
task_5.description: Conan 2.17.0 relaxes workspace path restrictions so packages and products can be registered even when their directories are outside the workspace root, and it adds workspace initialization and cleanup commands to support the updated workflow.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan workspaces can register, persist, and manage packages and products that are located outside the workspace directory, while preserving consistent workspace naming and safe cleanup behavior.

expectation.grounded: The workspace feature should accept absolute package, product, and output folder paths even when they resolve outside the workspace root, persist them in `conanws.yml` as normalized relative paths under the workspace package collection, and allow later removal using the same normalized path. `workspace clean` should iterate registered packages, remove each configured `output_folder`, skip packages without an `output_folder`, and warn instead of aborting when a folder cannot be removed. `workspace init` should be available as a CLI subcommand with an optional target path, and workspace naming should prefer an explicit workspace `name` value when present.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to keep a workspace file in one location and still register packages or products stored elsewhere on disk. Workspace lifecycle commands should support initializing a workspace, cleaning generated build output when defined, and showing a stable workspace name in user-visible output.

constraints.grounded: Workspace path registration must still require absolute input paths before they are normalized relative to the workspace. Relative paths may include parent-directory segments and must remain normalized for persistence, lookup, and removal. Removing an unregistered package path should still fail with the existing workspace error flow. Cleanup should only target declared package `output_folder` entries and should continue processing remaining packages after filesystem removal errors.
constraints.conceptual: The update should broaden valid workspace layouts without weakening validation of invalid path inputs, breaking removal semantics, or making cleanup destructive beyond explicitly configured build-output folders.

behavior: Workspace package and product registration no longer rejects locations simply because they are outside the workspace folder.
Stored workspace paths are normalized relative to the workspace directory, including parent-directory segments when needed.
Workspace package records are maintained in the package collection, and product entries use the same normalized relative path representation.
Removing a registered package also removes the matching product entry when that path is registered as a product.

The default `workspace clean` command removes each registered package `output_folder` when one is defined, reports packages that do not define one, and emits warnings for cleanup failures without terminating the whole clean operation.
`workspace init` is exposed as a CLI command that initializes a workspace at the provided path or in the current working directory when no path is given.
User-visible workspace naming prefers an explicit configured workspace name over the folder basename.
acceptance_criteria: When a package directory is outside the workspace folder, registering it in the workspace should succeed instead of failing solely because of its location.
When a product directory is outside the workspace folder, the workspace configuration should retain a normalized relative path that can later be used consistently by workspace operations.
When a registered package is removed by path, the workspace should remove the corresponding package entry and also remove that path from the product list if it was marked as a product.
When `workspace clean` runs and a registered package defines an `output_folder`, that folder should be removed as part of the clean operation.
When `workspace clean` encounters a registered package without an `output_folder`, it should skip that package and continue.
When one package output folder cannot be removed during `workspace clean`, the command should warn about that failure and continue cleaning the remaining packages.
When `workspace init` is run without an explicit path, it should initialize the workspace in the current directory; when a path is provided, it should initialize the workspace at that path.
When workspace metadata defines a workspace `name`, user-visible workspace output should use that name; otherwise it should use the workspace folder name.

task_7.title: Expand GCC version support to 13.4 and 14.3
task_7.description: Conan 2.17.0 expands its built-in GCC settings so newer GCC patch releases are recognized as supported compiler versions. This allows users to declare those toolchains in profiles and package settings without them being rejected as unknown values during normal settings validation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan accepts newer GCC patch releases, including GCC 14.3, in user-visible compiler settings so profiles and package configurations using those compilers are treated as valid.

expectation.grounded: When `compiler=gcc`, the built-in accepted `compiler.version` values should include `13.4` and `14.3` alongside the previously supported GCC versions. Any user flow that validates Conan settings against the default GCC version list should accept those values instead of rejecting them as unsupported or unknown.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to select newly supported GCC patch releases in their compiler configuration and have Conan recognize them anywhere compiler settings are checked.

constraints.grounded: Previously supported GCC `compiler.version` values must remain valid. The change should only extend the accepted GCC version list and must not alter validation behavior for non-GCC compilers or unrelated settings.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should broaden GCC compatibility without changing existing valid configurations or affecting unrelated compiler behavior.

behavior: Conan recognizes `13.4` as a valid `compiler.version` when `compiler=gcc`.
Conan recognizes `14.3` as a valid `compiler.version` when `compiler=gcc`.
Profiles, package settings, and other configuration inputs using those GCC versions can pass normal settings validation instead of failing because the version is not supported.
Existing supported GCC version values continue to behave as valid selections.
acceptance_criteria: When a user configures Conan with `compiler=gcc` and `compiler.version=13.4`, the configuration should be accepted as a valid GCC compiler version.
When a user configures Conan with `compiler=gcc` and `compiler.version=14.3`, the configuration should be accepted as a valid GCC compiler version.
When Conan validates profiles or package settings that specify either of those GCC versions, it should not fail solely because the GCC version is unknown or unsupported.
When users continue to use previously supported GCC versions, their configurations should remain valid after the upgrade.

task_9.title: Generate cl-like compiler cache entries in CMake presets for Ninja
task_9.description: Conan 2.17.0 updates CMakeToolchain preset generation so Windows MSVC-style Ninja builds can include explicit C and C++ compiler selections in generated CMake presets. This improves compiler activation for cl-like toolchains, including clang-cl, while avoiding broader changes for other compiler families or generators.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeToolchain-generated presets automatically define the active C and C++ compiler for MSVC cl-like toolchains when using the Ninja generator, so consumers can configure builds with the intended compiler without manual preset edits.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeToolchain generates presets, it should populate CMAKE_C_COMPILER and CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER in preset cache variables only for supported cl-like compilers. The compiler values should come from tools.build:compiler_executables for the c and cpp languages when provided, and otherwise default to cl for MSVC configurations using a Ninja generator. This behavior applies only when the resolved compiler executable name is cl, cl.exe, clang-cl, or clang-cl.exe.
expectation.conceptual: Generated CMake presets should automatically carry the intended C and C++ compiler for Windows MSVC-style Ninja builds, including clang-cl workflows, so CMake sees the correct compiler during configuration.

constraints.grounded: Do not add CMAKE_C_COMPILER or CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER through this feature for non-cl-like executables. Do not auto-default compiler entries outside MSVC configurations that use the Ninja generator. Existing preset content, including other cache variables and the toolchain file reference, must remain unaffected.
constraints.conceptual: The automatic compiler injection should stay narrowly scoped to supported MSVC-style compiler flows and must not change unrelated generators or non-MSVC compiler configurations.

behavior: Generated presets now add CMAKE_C_COMPILER when the configured or inferred C compiler is a supported cl-like executable.
Generated presets now add CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER when the configured or inferred C++ compiler is a supported cl-like executable.
Configured compiler executables from tools.build:compiler_executables take precedence over automatic defaults for the c and cpp languages.
For MSVC configurations using the Ninja generator, missing c and cpp compiler entries may be inferred as cl.
Compiler executables whose basename is not one of the supported cl-like names are excluded from these preset cache variable additions.
acceptance_criteria: When CMakeToolchain generates a preset for an MSVC configuration using the Ninja generator and no explicit c or cpp compiler executables are configured, the preset should include CMAKE_C_COMPILER and CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER set to cl.

When tools.build:compiler_executables sets the c and cpp compilers to clang-cl for a Ninja-based MSVC-style build, the generated preset should include CMAKE_C_COMPILER and CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER using clang-cl.
When configured compiler executables for c or cpp are not cl-like, the generated preset should not add CMAKE_C_COMPILER or CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER for those languages through this behavior.
When the generator is not Ninja, the preset should not infer cl as the default compiler solely because the compiler is MSVC.

task_8.title: Add default C standard detection
task_8.description: Version 2.17.0 adds user-facing support for detecting the default C language standard associated with a compiler and compiler version. The upgrade exposes this capability through the build tools API so recipes can query Conan for the inferred default C standard instead of hardcoding it, while leaving unsupported compilers unresolved rather than guessing.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan can report the default C language standard for the active compiler/version combination so recipes can reason about `compiler.cstd` consistently during an upgrade from 2.16.1 to 2.17.0.

expectation.grounded: Expose `default_cstd(conanfile, compiler=None, compiler_version=None)` from `conan.tools.build`. The function should use the explicit `compiler` and `compiler_version` arguments when provided, otherwise read `compiler` and `compiler.version` from the recipe settings. It should return the inferred default `compiler.cstd` for supported compilers: `gcc` returns `gnu99` before version 5, `gnu11` for versions 5 through 7, `gnu17` for versions 8 through 14, and `gnu23` from version 15 onward; `clang` returns `gnu99` before version 4, `gnu11` for versions 4 through 10, and `gnu17` from version 11 onward; `apple-clang` returns `gnu99` before version 10, `gnu11` for versions 10 and 11, and `gnu17` from version 12 onward. For `msvc`, `intel-cc`, and `mcst-lcc`, the function should return `None`. If compiler identity or compiler version is unavailable, it should raise `ConanException` instead of inferring a value.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading should be able to ask Conan for the default C standard implied by a compiler and version, either from the current recipe settings or from explicit inputs. Conan should return a normalized default standard when it knows the compiler family behavior, return no inferred default for compiler families it cannot determine safely, and fail clearly when the compiler context is incomplete.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to default C standard inference and API exposure. It must not require callers to set `compiler.cstd` explicitly before querying, must not fabricate defaults for unsupported compiler families, and must not override a user-selected standard as part of the lookup. The exported symbol should be available alongside the existing C standard helpers in `conan.tools.build`.
constraints.conceptual: The new capability is informational rather than prescriptive. It should help recipes understand compiler defaults without changing explicit user configuration, and it should stay conservative by avoiding guesses for compilers whose default C standard is not defined by the feature.

behavior: A new public build-tools helper is available to query the default `compiler.cstd` for a compiler/version pair.
The helper accepts either explicit compiler inputs or falls back to the current recipe settings when those inputs are omitted.
For supported compiler families, the returned default C standard changes by compiler version according to Conan's built-in mapping for `gcc`, `clang`, and `apple-clang`.
For `msvc`, `intel-cc`, and `mcst-lcc`, the helper reports that no default C standard is inferred by returning `None`.
Calling the helper without a resolvable compiler or compiler version produces `ConanException` instead of silently returning an inferred value.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe calls `conan.tools.build.default_cstd()` with `compiler=gcc` and a version earlier than 5, it should receive `gnu99`; with version 5 through 7 it should receive `gnu11`; with version 8 through 14 it should receive `gnu17`; and with version 15 or newer it should receive `gnu23`.
When a recipe calls `conan.tools.build.default_cstd()` with `compiler=clang`, it should receive `gnu99` before version 4, `gnu11` for versions 4 through 10, and `gnu17` for version 11 and newer.
When a recipe calls `conan.tools.build.default_cstd()` with `compiler=apple-clang`, it should receive `gnu99` before version 10, `gnu11` for versions 10 and 11, and `gnu17` for version 12 and newer.
When a recipe calls `conan.tools.build.default_cstd()` for `msvc`, `intel-cc`, or `mcst-lcc`, it should return `None` rather than an inferred standard.

When explicit `compiler` and `compiler_version` arguments are omitted, `conan.tools.build.default_cstd()` should derive them from the recipe settings and return the same result as if they had been passed directly.
When neither explicit inputs nor recipe settings provide both compiler identity and compiler version, `conan.tools.build.default_cstd()` should fail with `ConanException`.

task_10.title: Add a built-in header-only library template to conan new
task_10.description: The upgrade adds a new built-in `header_lib` template to `conan new` so users can scaffold header-only Conan packages with standard package metadata, packaged headers, optional requirements, and a generated consumer example based on CMake.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan new` provides a built-in `header_lib` template for creating header-only library packages, including package metadata, exported headers, optional declared requirements, and a generated example consumer project.

expectation.grounded: `conan new` must accept `header_lib` as a built-in template name. Generating this template must produce a Conan recipe configured as a `header-library` package, export headers from an `include` directory, use `auto_header_only` package ID behavior, package the exported headers, and expose no binary or library directories in `package_info()`. When `requires` values are provided to the template, the generated recipe must add them in `requirements()`, and the generated public header must reference and invoke those dependencies consistently with the template's package naming. The generated consumer example must use CMake integration through `CMakeDeps` and `CMakeToolchain`, locate the package with `find_package`, link against the package target, and run the example executable when the environment supports execution.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to scaffold a header-only Conan package directly from `conan new` without starting from a generic template. The generated project should behave like a standard header-only package: headers are exported and packaged, package identity does not vary by build settings, no binary or library folders are advertised, optional dependencies can be declared at generation time, and the sample consumer project should demonstrate consuming the package through Conan's CMake integration.

constraints.grounded: The change must remain additive to the existing `conan new` built-in templates and CLI help. The `header_lib` template must model a header-only package rather than a compiled library, so it must not require library artifacts, binary directories, or compiled outputs from the package itself. Optional dependency support must only affect generated output when `requires` input is provided. The generated consumer example must depend on the created package through the tested reference and only attempt execution when runnable on the current platform.
constraints.conceptual: This should extend template generation without changing existing templates. The generated scaffold must reflect header-only packaging semantics, avoid implying compiled library outputs, and handle optional dependencies only when the user supplies them. The included example should be usable as a normal consumer example and avoid assuming the executable can always run in every environment.

behavior: `conan new` recognizes `header_lib` as a documented built-in template option.
Generating `header_lib` creates a Conan package recipe whose package type is header-only and whose packaged contents come from exported headers.
The generated recipe applies automatic header-only package ID behavior so build settings and options do not define distinct binary package identities.
The generated recipe clears binary and library directory metadata from `cpp_info` to reflect that the package ships headers only.
If template `requires` values are supplied, the generated recipe adds those requirements and the generated header references the dependency headers and invokes their exported entry points.
The generated scaffold includes an `include` header implementing the package's sample API and a test package that consumes the package through Conan's CMake generators.
The generated consumer project finds the package via CMake package discovery, links against the package target, builds an example executable, and runs it only when execution is supported.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan new header_lib` with a package name and version, it should generate a complete header-only package scaffold instead of rejecting the template name.
When the generated recipe is inspected, it should identify the package as header-only, export and package headers from the generated include tree, and avoid advertising binary or library directories.
When the template is generated without extra requirements, it should produce a self-contained header-only package scaffold and example consumer project.
When the template is generated with one or more `requires` values, the generated recipe should declare those dependencies and the generated public header should integrate with them in the sample API.
When the generated consumer example is built in a runnable environment, it should consume the package through Conan's CMake integration and execute the example program successfully.

task_12.title: Expose subprocess in Jinja profile rendering
task_12.description: Conan 2.17.0 extends profile Jinja rendering so templates can access Python's subprocess module at render time. This lets profile values be derived from external command execution in addition to the existing platform and os helpers.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Jinja-rendered Conan profiles can use the `subprocess` module during template evaluation so profile values can be computed from external command output when needed.

expectation.grounded: During profile template rendering, the Jinja context should expose `subprocess` alongside the existing rendering helpers so profile authors can call public `subprocess` APIs from profile expressions. Profile rendering should therefore accept templates that reference `subprocess` and evaluate them at render time instead of failing because the name is unavailable.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to write dynamic profile templates that invoke external commands while the profile is being rendered. A profile that uses `subprocess` in its Jinja expressions should render successfully and produce configuration values based on the command result.

constraints.grounded: This change is limited to the Jinja rendering context for Conan profiles. Existing context entries such as `platform`, `os`, `profile_dir`, `profile_name`, `conan_version`, and detected settings should remain available and unchanged in behavior while adding `subprocess` as an additional rendering symbol.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should add one new template capability without removing or altering the profile features users already rely on. Existing profile templates should keep working as before, and only templates that choose to use `subprocess` should observe the new behavior.

behavior: Jinja evaluation of Conan profiles now includes the `subprocess` module in the template context.
Profile templates may call public `subprocess` APIs while computing settings, options, or other rendered values.
A profile template that references `subprocess` should no longer fail due to that symbol being missing from the rendering environment.
Previously available rendering helpers remain present while `subprocess` is added as an extra context object.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan profile contains a Jinja expression that references `subprocess`, the profile should render successfully if the expression itself is otherwise valid.
When a Jinja profile uses `subprocess` to obtain data from an external command, the rendered profile output should reflect the command result in the resulting profile values.
When rendering a profile that does not use `subprocess`, existing Jinja-based profile behavior should remain unchanged.
When rendering a profile that uses existing helpers such as `platform` or `os` together with `subprocess`, all referenced helpers should be available in the same rendering context.

task_11.title: Expand Meson standard flag generation
task_11.description: Meson standard helper behavior was broadened so Conan can generate C and C++ standard flags from configured values instead of relying on a fixed hardcoded subset. This makes newer and GNU-prefixed standards resolve correctly while leaving unset standards without a flag.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Meson C and C++ standard flag generation supports configured standard values beyond a fixed predefined subset, including GNU dialects and newer language versions, while leaving the flag unset when no standard is configured.

expectation.grounded: For Meson integrations that use `to_cppstd_flag(compiler, compiler_version, cppstd)` and `to_cstd_flag(cstd)`, the helpers should return `None` when the corresponding standard value is unset. For non-MSVC C++ configurations, `to_cppstd_flag` should derive Meson-compatible flags directly from the requested standard, producing GNU C++ forms for `gnu`-prefixed values and ISO C++ forms for non-GNU values instead of limiting support to a fixed lookup table. `to_cstd_flag` should preserve GNU C standard names and convert non-GNU values to Meson `c` standard names. MSVC-specific C++ flag resolution should continue to follow its compiler-version-aware behavior.
expectation.conceptual: When Meson toolchain generation is given a C or C++ language standard, it should emit the matching Meson standard setting for that requested mode, including newer standard versions and GNU dialects. If no language standard is configured, no standard flag should be produced.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress existing Meson standard outputs for already supported C and C++ values. Preserve the distinction between GNU and non-GNU standard modes for non-MSVC C and C++ settings. Keep MSVC C++ handling aligned with its existing version-dependent mapping rather than forcing it into the generic non-MSVC format.
constraints.conceptual: Existing standard selections should keep working, GNU dialect requests should stay GNU dialect requests, and compiler-specific behavior should remain intact where special handling already exists.

behavior: `to_cppstd_flag` now returns no flag when `cppstd` is unset.
For non-MSVC C++ configurations, `to_cppstd_flag` derives Meson ISO C++ standard names from the requested standard value instead of relying on a fixed list of known versions.
For non-MSVC GNU C++ configurations, `to_cppstd_flag` preserves GNU dialect semantics by emitting Meson GNU C++ standard names derived from the requested value.
`to_cstd_flag` returns no flag when `cstd` is unset.
`to_cstd_flag` preserves GNU-prefixed C standard values and converts non-GNU C standard values into Meson C standard names.
MSVC C++ standard resolution remains compiler-version aware and separate from the generic Meson C++ flag formatting used for other compilers.
acceptance_criteria: When a non-MSVC C++ standard is configured with an ISO value such as `23` or another supported future numeric version, Meson flag generation should produce the corresponding ISO C++ standard name instead of failing because the value is not in a hardcoded subset.

When a non-MSVC C++ standard is configured with a GNU value such as `gnu23`, Meson flag generation should produce the corresponding GNU C++ standard name and should not downgrade it to a non-GNU mode.
When a C standard is configured with an ISO value such as `23`, Meson flag generation should produce the corresponding Meson C standard name.
When a C standard is configured with a GNU value such as `gnu23`, Meson flag generation should preserve that GNU C standard name.
When no C or C++ standard is configured, the corresponding helper should produce no standard flag.
When MSVC is the active C++ compiler, the generated C++ standard flag should continue to follow MSVC-specific Meson mapping behavior.

task_14.title: Add verbose progress output for conan cache clean
task_14.description: Upgrading to 2.17.0 adds verbose progress logging to `conan cache clean` so long-running cache cleanup operations expose what is being cleaned instead of appearing idle, without changing the cleanup targets themselves.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan cache clean` provides visible progress updates in verbose mode while cleaning cache contents, so users can tell the command is actively processing temporary folders, backup sources, recipes, and packages.

expectation.grounded: When `conan cache clean` runs with verbose output enabled, it should emit verbose log entries before cleaning temporary folders, before removing backup sources with the number of backup-source entries selected, once per recipe reference before cleaning recipe cache contents, and once per package reference before cleaning package cache contents. The command's cleanup selection and deletion behavior should otherwise remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Users who opt into verbose output for cache cleanup should see clear progress information for each major cleanup stage and each targeted recipe or package, making long-running cleanup work observable rather than silent.

constraints.grounded: The new output must be informational only. It must not alter which recipe or package references are selected, which source/build/download/backup artifacts are removed, or the cleanup behavior of non-verbose executions.
constraints.conceptual: The enhancement should improve visibility only. It must not change the meaning of the command, the cleanup scope, or the behavior users get when they do not request verbose output.

behavior: `conan cache clean` emits a verbose progress line before scanning and deleting temporary build folders that are not associated with stored package metadata.
When backup source cleanup is requested, the command emits a verbose progress line reporting how many backup source entries are being cleaned, including when that count is zero.
For each selected recipe reference, the command emits a verbose line indicating that recipe cache contents are being cleaned before recipe-level source or download cleanup occurs.
For each selected package reference under a recipe, the command emits a verbose line indicating that package cache contents are being cleaned before package-level build or download cleanup occurs.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan cache clean` with verbose output enabled and temporary folders are eligible for cleanup, the command should print a progress update before removing those temporary folders.
When a user requests backup source cleanup in verbose mode, the command should report the number of backup source entries being cleaned, even when there are none.
When verbose mode is enabled and the cleanup target includes recipe references, the command should print a recipe-scoped progress update for each selected recipe reference.
When verbose mode is enabled and the cleanup target includes package references, the command should print a package-scoped progress update for each selected package reference.
When the command is run without verbose output, it should preserve existing cleanup behavior without the new progress reporting.

task_13.title: Add source exclusion and slimmer cache-save archives
task_13.description: Upgrading to Conan 2.17.0 changes `conan cache save` so cache snapshots can optionally omit recipe sources with `--no-source`, and saved archives now contain only restorable recipe, package, and metadata content instead of bundling transient downloaded artifacts.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan cache save` can produce smaller, portable cache archives by excluding transient downloaded artifacts from saved snapshots and by allowing users to omit recipe sources when they do not want them included.

expectation.grounded: `conan cache save` must accept a `--no-source` option. By default, `conan cache save` should archive the selected recipe export content, exported sources, recipe source contents, package contents, and available metadata needed for restore. When `--no-source` is provided, the saved archive should omit recipe source contents while still preserving the selected recipes, packages, and metadata. The generated archive must no longer include downloaded cache artifacts such as nested recipe or package `.tgz` downloads.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to create cache backups that restore usable recipes and packages without carrying redundant downloaded blobs, and they should be able to intentionally exclude recipe sources to keep the archive smaller.

constraints.grounded: Existing package selection and output-file behavior of `conan cache save` should remain intact. Source contents should still be included unless `--no-source` is explicitly requested. Cache restore compatibility must be preserved for the retained recipe, package, and metadata contents, and transient downloaded artifacts must not be reintroduced into saved archives.
constraints.conceptual: The new option must be opt-in, existing save/restore workflows should keep working for actual restorable content, and the archive should stay focused on durable cache state rather than temporary downloaded data.

behavior: `conan cache save` accepts a `--no-source` flag that excludes recipe source contents from the generated cache archive.
Without `--no-source`, saved cache archives continue to include recipe sources alongside exported recipe files, exported sources, package payloads, and available metadata.
Saved cache archives no longer recursively bundle downloaded recipe or package archive artifacts into the output `.tgz`.
Restoring a cache archive created by `conan cache save` should recover the selected recipes, packages, and metadata without restoring those transient downloaded artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan cache save` for selected references without `--no-source`, the resulting archive should restore the selected recipes, packages, metadata, and recipe source contents.
When a user runs `conan cache save` with `--no-source`, the resulting archive should restore the selected recipes, packages, and metadata but should not restore recipe source contents.

When the selected cache entries contain downloaded recipe or package `.tgz` artifacts, saving and restoring through `conan cache save` should not reproduce those downloaded artifacts in the restored cache.
When users save cache snapshots after this upgrade, the archive should remain usable for `conan cache restore` while avoiding redundant transient cache content.

task_15.title: Support package-list input for cache maintenance commands
task_15.description: Conan 2.17.0 adds package-list based targeting to cache maintenance commands so users can clean or verify specific local cache entries without relying only on reference patterns. The update also defines clear validation rules for how list-based and pattern-based selection may be used.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan cache clean` and `conan cache check-integrity` support selecting local cache entries from a package list file via `--list`, so users can run these operations on an explicit cache selection instead of only a reference pattern.

expectation.grounded: `conan cache clean` and `conan cache check-integrity` must accept `-l/--list` as an alternative selection input that loads target entries from a package list file. `conan cache clean` must continue to allow an omitted `pattern` and treat the no-list case as `*`. `conan cache check-integrity` must allow either a `pattern` or `--list`, but raise a `ConanException` if both are omitted. Both commands must raise a `ConanException` if `pattern` and `--list` are provided together. When `--list` is used, the commands must operate on the local-cache entries from that package list instead of resolving the selection from `pattern` and `--package-query`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to provide a package list file to both cache-cleaning and cache-integrity commands and have the command act on exactly that explicit local-cache selection. Pattern-based selection should still work as before, but the CLI should reject ambiguous or incomplete selection inputs.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress the existing pattern-based behavior of `conan cache clean` when `--list` is absent, including the implicit all-cache selection behavior. `conan cache check-integrity` must not run without an explicit selection source. Neither command may accept list-based and pattern-based selection in the same invocation.
constraints.conceptual: Existing wildcard and pattern workflows should remain intact, while the new list-based workflow must behave as a mutually exclusive alternative. The commands should fail fast when the user input is contradictory or missing.

behavior: `conan cache clean` accepts `-l/--list` to select cache entries from a package list file for cleaning operations.
`conan cache check-integrity` accepts `-l/--list` to select cache entries from a package list file for integrity verification.
Providing both a positional selection pattern and `--list` to either command causes the command to raise a `ConanException` instead of running.
`conan cache check-integrity` allows the positional selection pattern to be omitted only when `--list` is supplied; if both are omitted, it raises a `ConanException`.
When `--list` is not supplied, `conan cache clean` continues to resolve targets from the selection pattern and defaults to the existing all-cache behavior.
When `--list` is supplied, target selection comes from the package list file's local-cache entries rather than from pattern-based lookup.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan cache clean --list <package-list>` with cache-cleaning options, the command should clean the local cache entries identified by that package list.
When a user runs `conan cache check-integrity --list <package-list>`, the command should perform integrity checks on the local cache entries identified by that package list.
When a user passes both a selection pattern and `--list` to either command, the command should fail with a `ConanException` and should not execute the cache operation.
When a user runs `conan cache check-integrity` without a selection pattern and without `--list`, the command should fail with a `ConanException` instead of proceeding.
When a user runs `conan cache clean` without a selection pattern and without `--list`, the command should continue to behave according to the existing implicit all-cache selection.

task_17.title: Expose upload URLs in conan upload JSON output
task_17.description: The 2.17.0 update extends `conan upload` JSON output so users and automation can see the remote destination URL and checksum for each uploaded recipe or package file. This adds observable metadata to the existing upload report without changing the command surface.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan upload` JSON output includes per-file upload destination information so users and tooling can identify where each uploaded recipe and package artifact is stored and verify the associated file content.

expectation.grounded: When `conan upload` produces JSON output, each recipe revision bundle and each package revision bundle that contains `files` should also expose an `upload-urls` object keyed by the same file names. Every `upload-urls` entry should provide the remote file URL for that artifact and a checksum of the uploaded local file content. Recipe entries should resolve against the recipe file route for the selected remote, and package entries should resolve against the package file route for the selected remote.
expectation.conceptual: The upload report should let consumers inspect, for every uploaded artifact, the final remote location and integrity metadata in a machine-readable form. Both recipe-level and package-level uploads should expose this information consistently in the JSON result.

constraints.grounded: The new metadata should augment the existing JSON structure instead of replacing current `files` information. `upload-urls` should only be emitted for artifacts that are present in the upload result, and generated URLs should remain well-formed regardless of whether the configured remote URL includes a trailing slash.
constraints.conceptual: Existing upload JSON data should continue to work, with the new URL metadata added as an extension. The feature should not invent entries for nonexistent artifacts or produce malformed destination links.

behavior: `conan upload` JSON output now includes an `upload-urls` mapping for uploaded recipe files.
`conan upload` JSON output now includes an `upload-urls` mapping for uploaded package files.
Each `upload-urls` entry is keyed by artifact file name and exposes the remote destination URL plus a checksum for that file.
The destination URL is derived from the selected remote and corresponds to the artifact type, using recipe file endpoints for recipe artifacts and package file endpoints for package artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan upload` is executed with JSON output enabled for a recipe upload, the JSON result should include an `upload-urls` object for the recipe revision containing one entry per reported recipe file.

When `conan upload` is executed with JSON output enabled for a package upload, the JSON result should include an `upload-urls` object for the package revision containing one entry per reported package file.
When an `upload-urls` entry is present, it should include both the remote file URL and a checksum value for that artifact.
When the configured remote base URL has or lacks a trailing slash, the emitted upload URLs should still be valid and should not contain malformed duplicate separators.

task_16.title: Expose remote allowed_packages in JSON output
task_16.description: The upgrade adds package allowlist metadata to the JSON representation of configured remotes so automation and integrations can inspect remote restrictions without relying on non-JSON output or separate configuration lookups.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that remote information exported in JSON includes each remote's configured package allowlist so users and tooling can detect remote package restrictions directly from the JSON output.

expectation.grounded: When remotes are emitted in JSON form, every remote object should include an `allowed_packages` field in addition to the existing `name`, `url`, `verify_ssl`, and `enabled` fields. The `allowed_packages` value should reflect the remote's configured allowlist state for package patterns.
expectation.conceptual: JSON remote listings should expose whether a remote is restricted to specific packages, so users and automation can read the remote's package access scope from the same JSON payload as the rest of the remote metadata.

constraints.grounded: The change must be additive for JSON remote entries: existing fields and their semantics remain available, and `allowed_packages` should be present for each remote entry rather than only for selected remotes.
constraints.conceptual: Existing JSON consumers should continue to receive the same remote data as before, with one additional field that consistently communicates package restriction metadata.

behavior: Remote JSON output includes a new `allowed_packages` property for every remote entry.
The `allowed_packages` property mirrors the configured package allowlist associated with that remote.
Previously exposed remote metadata such as name, URL, SSL verification status, and enabled state remains part of the JSON output with unchanged meaning.
Consumers of remote JSON output can determine remote package restriction scope without consulting separate command output.
acceptance_criteria: When a remote has package allowlist rules configured and remotes are requested in JSON format, the corresponding JSON object should include `allowed_packages` populated with that remote's configured restriction data.

When a remote has no package allowlist configured and remotes are requested in JSON format, the corresponding JSON object should still include `allowed_packages` representing the remote's unconfigured or empty allowlist state.
When remotes are requested in JSON format, the JSON output should still include the pre-existing remote fields and preserve their observable behavior while adding `allowed_packages`.

task_20.title: Update conan audit guidance links
task_20.description: Version 2.17.0 updates the user-facing links shown by `conan audit` so vulnerability and rate-limit guidance points to the current Conan audit and JFrog Catalog pages instead of outdated JFrog security marketing URLs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan audit` surfaces current, relevant help URLs when showing vulnerability results or rate-limit guidance, so users are directed to the active Conan audit documentation pages instead of obsolete product pages.

expectation.grounded: When `conan audit` prints vulnerability information, the footer should identify JFrog Catalog as the source and direct users to `https://audit.conan.io/jfrogcuration`. When the Conan Center audit provider reports rate limiting, the follow-up help link should direct users to `https://audit.conan.io/limit` instead of an older JFrog DevSecOps page.
expectation.conceptual: The audit CLI should present up-to-date support and product information links wherever it explains vulnerability results or request limits, so users land on the correct current documentation and service pages.

constraints.grounded: This upgrade is limited to the observable guidance shown by `conan audit`; it should not change vulnerability counting, audit result rendering, error handling, or the existing support contact guidance beyond updating the referenced destination pages.
constraints.conceptual: Only the user-facing references should change. The audit command's functional behavior, results, and existing support flow should otherwise remain the same.

behavior: Successful or partially successful `conan audit` vulnerability output now attributes vulnerability data to JFrog Catalog rather than the older JFrog Advanced Security naming.
The vulnerability information footer shown by `conan audit` now points users to `https://audit.conan.io/jfrogcuration` for more information.
When audit requests hit the Conan Center provider rate limit, the guidance link shown to the user now points to `https://audit.conan.io/limit`.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan audit` displays vulnerability information, it should include a current informational link to `https://audit.conan.io/jfrogcuration`.
When `conan audit` displays vulnerability information, it should refer to JFrog Catalog as the provider of that information.
When the Conan Center audit provider informs the user that request limits have been exceeded, the displayed help URL should be `https://audit.conan.io/limit`.
When upgrading to 2.17.0, users should no longer be directed from audit output to the previous JFrog Advanced Security or JFrog DevSecOps marketing URLs for these cases.

task_19.title: Fix Conan PyInstaller packaging to exclude test modules correctly
task_19.description: The PyInstaller packaging flow for Conan was adjusted so standalone executables collect the Conan runtime more reliably while excluding the full conan.test module tree. This prevents false missing-import failures from test-only modules during executable builds and ensures required bundled imports are still available at runtime.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan executables built with the PyInstaller integration package the Conan runtime without traversing Conan test-only modules, so users do not see spurious missing-import failures from conan.test subpackages during build or due to omitted bundled imports at runtime.

expectation.grounded: The PyInstaller packaging flow invoked by `pyinstall()` should collect Conan submodules for bundling, exclude the full `conan.test.*` package tree from module collection, and forward hidden imports as explicit `--hidden-import` entries, including the standard-library modules `glob` and `pathlib`. Building the executable should no longer surface unresolved hidden-import failures caused by discovery of `conan.test.utils.*` modules.
expectation.conceptual: Building the standalone Conan executable with PyInstaller should include the modules needed for normal Conan usage, omit Conan's test-only packages, and avoid packaging-time or runtime import failures that come from PyInstaller trying to bundle internal test modules.

constraints.grounded: The exclusion must apply to the entire `conan.test` subtree, not just the package root. Existing non-test hidden imports must still be passed through individually to PyInstaller, and current packaging variants such as one-file builds and Windows version metadata handling must remain unaffected.
constraints.conceptual: Only test-only Conan modules should be excluded. Normal Conan functionality and existing supported packaging modes must continue to work after the upgrade.

behavior: The PyInstaller invocation now requests collection of Conan submodules as part of packaging the executable.
The `conan.test` package tree is excluded with wildcard coverage so nested test utility modules are not discovered as bundle dependencies.
Hidden imports are emitted as discrete PyInstaller hidden-import arguments instead of relying on a precomposed split string.
The bundled executable explicitly includes the standard-library imports `glob` and `pathlib` needed by the packaged Conan runtime.
PyInstaller builds no longer produce false missing hidden-import failures for `conan.test.utils.*` modules caused by scanning Conan test packages.
acceptance_criteria: When a user builds a Conan executable through the PyInstaller integration, the build should exclude the `conan.test` subtree instead of attempting to bundle nested test utility modules.
When PyInstaller analyzes the Conan package for that build, it should not report missing hidden-import failures for `conan.test.utils.*` modules that were only reached through test-package discovery.
When the resulting executable runs Conan code paths that depend on packaged standard-library imports, it should not fail because `glob` or `pathlib` were omitted from the bundle.
When users build with existing supported packaging options such as one-file mode or Windows version metadata, those options should continue to work with the updated PyInstaller packaging flow.

task_18.title: Add workspace initialization and clean support for editable package workspaces
task_18.description: The update adds first-class workspace lifecycle support around editable packages. Users can initialize a workspace scaffold, run a dedicated workspace clean command to remove configured output folders, and optionally provide custom cleanup behavior from the workspace definition, while workspace metadata now treats editable entries as packages and supports relative package locations.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan workspaces can be initialized and cleaned from the CLI, that default cleanup removes only configured output folders for workspace packages, and that workspace package metadata remains usable for packages referenced by relative paths, including paths outside the workspace directory.

expectation.grounded: Expose `conan workspace init [path]` to create the target workspace directory and create `conanws.yml` and a minimal `conanws.py` only when they do not already exist. Expose `conan workspace clean` for the active workspace and dispatch it through `Workspace.clean()`. In the default `Workspace` implementation, iterate over workspace `packages`, remove each package `output_folder` when defined, skip packages without an `output_folder`, and emit warnings instead of aborting when folder deletion raises `OSError`. Workspace state and info should use `packages` entries rather than `editables`, permit relative package paths that resolve outside the workspace root, and use the `name` defined in `conanws.yml` when present as the workspace display/output scope.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to bootstrap a workspace, register workspace packages from nearby folders, and clean generated build/output directories from the workspace CLI. Cleanup should follow workspace-specific behavior when the workspace defines its own clean routine; otherwise it should remove only the configured output directories and leave packages without such directories unchanged.

constraints.grounded: Default workspace cleaning must not remove package source directories or alter package/product registration; it is limited to deleting configured `output_folder` directories. Initialization must be non-destructive for existing `conanws.yml` and `conanws.py` files. Workspace path normalization must continue to resolve package entries by normalized relative paths, including entries outside the workspace folder. Cleanup must tolerate missing `output_folder` values and per-package removal failures without terminating the whole command.
constraints.conceptual: Initialization should not overwrite an existing workspace definition. Cleanup should be limited to generated output folders, not package sources or workspace membership. Workspace commands should continue working when packages live outside the workspace folder, and one cleanup problem should not stop the rest of the workspace from being processed.

behavior: `conan workspace clean` becomes an available CLI subcommand for the current workspace.
The default workspace cleanup removes each registered workspace package's configured `output_folder` relative to the workspace location.
Workspace packages that do not declare an `output_folder` are skipped during cleanup rather than treated as an error.
If deleting one package output folder fails with an OS-level removal error, the command reports a warning and continues processing other packages.
A workspace-defined `Workspace.clean()` implementation in `conanws.py` can supply custom cleanup behavior for `conan workspace clean`.
`conan workspace init` can scaffold a workspace directory by creating `conanws.yml` and a minimal `conanws.py` when those files are absent.
Workspace metadata and info now expose package entries under `packages` instead of `editables`.
Workspace package paths can be stored and resolved as relative references even when the package is located outside the workspace directory.
When a workspace `name` is declared in `conanws.yml`, that name is used as the workspace identity for user-visible workspace output.
acceptance_criteria: Given a workspace package with an `output_folder`, when `conan workspace clean` is run, the configured output directory should be removed.

Given a workspace package without an `output_folder`, when `conan workspace clean` is run, the command should leave that package unchanged and complete without treating the missing output folder as a failure.
Given multiple workspace packages, when one output folder cannot be removed, the command should surface a warning for that package and continue cleaning the remaining packages.
Given a workspace that defines its own `Workspace.clean()` in `conanws.py`, when `conan workspace clean` is run, the workspace-specific cleanup behavior should execute.
Given a target folder that does not yet contain workspace files, when `conan workspace init` is run, the workspace scaffold should be created without overwriting pre-existing workspace files.

Given a workspace whose configuration declares a `name` and references packages through relative paths outside the workspace folder, workspace operations should retain those package references and use the configured workspace name in user-visible output.

task_23.title: Clarify unzip extraction output wording
task_23.description: The archive extraction helper now reports a more accurate user-facing status message when handling supported compressed archives. This aligns the `unzip()` tool's console output with the broader set of archive formats it can extract, without changing the extraction API or decompression behavior itself.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that archive extraction status output from the unzip tool uses wording that correctly describes uncompressing supported archive formats rather than implying ZIP-only behavior.

expectation.grounded: Calling `conan.tools.files.unzip()` should continue to perform the same extraction flow for supported archives, but the informational output emitted through the Conan output stream before extraction should describe the action as archive uncompression instead of unzip-specific terminology. This applies regardless of whether the input is a ZIP archive or a tar-based compressed archive handled by the same API.
expectation.conceptual: When users invoke the archive extraction helper, the status text they see should accurately describe a generic archive decompression operation, so the output is correct for all supported archive types and not misleadingly ZIP-specific.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the public `unzip()` API shape, supported archive handling branches, destination semantics, permission handling, filtering behavior, or extraction side effects. Only the observable wording of the informational extraction message should change.
constraints.conceptual: The update should be non-disruptive: archive extraction should behave exactly as before, with the only user-visible change being clearer status wording during extraction.

behavior: The archive extraction helper emits an informational status line before extraction begins.
That status line now uses neutral archive-decompression wording rather than unzip-specific wording.
The wording change applies to all supported archive types processed through the same extraction entry point, including tar-based compressed archives.
No extraction results, parameters, or archive-processing behavior are otherwise changed by this update.
acceptance_criteria: When a user invokes `conan.tools.files.unzip()` on a supported archive, it should still extract the archive to the requested destination as before.
When `conan.tools.files.unzip()` reports its pre-extraction status, it should describe the operation as uncompressing the archive rather than unzipping it.
When the input archive is a tar-based compressed format supported by `unzip()`, the emitted status wording should still be generic and accurate for that format.
When existing consumers rely on `unzip()` extraction behavior, they should observe no behavioral change other than the updated informational wording.

task_22.title: Support Windows LLVM/Clang frontends in GNU-style toolchains
task_22.description: Conan 2.17.0 fixes Windows LLVM/Clang support for GNU-style build flows so users can build with either the GNU-compatible clang frontend or the MSVC-compatible clang-cl frontend. The update aligns generated compiler, linker, and runtime flags with the selected frontend and MSVC runtime model.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Windows builds using Conan's GNU-style toolchains work correctly when `compiler=clang` is configured with either `clang` or `clang-cl`, and that the generated compile and link flags match the selected LLVM/Clang frontend and MSVC runtime behavior.

expectation.grounded: When `tools.build:compiler_executables` selects LLVM/Clang on Windows with `compiler=clang`, Conan should distinguish between the GNU-compatible `clang` frontend and the MSVC-compatible `clang-cl` frontend. `AutotoolsToolchain` and `GnuToolchain` should emit frontend-appropriate flags: `cppstd_flag()` should use the `clang-cl` form for standard selection, and Windows `clang` builds targeting the MSVC runtime should receive compatible runtime and linker flags so generated build environments and link flags produce successful builds with the expected MSVC runtime library.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to switch between `clang` and `clang-cl` on Windows without hand-fixing Conan's generated GNU-style toolchain flags. Standard-selection, runtime-library, and linker behavior should automatically match the chosen frontend so builds complete with the intended runtime linkage.

constraints.grounded: The frontend-specific behavior should apply only to Windows configurations using `compiler=clang` with MSVC-style runtime settings available. Existing behavior for non-Windows targets, non-clang compilers, and unaffected clang configurations should remain unchanged. Dynamic and static MSVC runtime modes must continue to map to the correct runtime-linkage behavior without introducing extra runtime flags where the selected frontend already defaults appropriately.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped to the affected Windows LLVM/Clang cases and must not regress other compiler or platform configurations. Runtime selection should stay consistent with the user's chosen static or dynamic MSVC runtime mode.

behavior: Conan detects whether Windows `compiler=clang` is using the GNU-compatible `clang` frontend or the MSVC-compatible `clang-cl` frontend from `tools.build:compiler_executables`.
For `clang-cl`, generated C++ standard flags use the frontend-compatible standard-selection syntax instead of the GNU-style form.

For Windows builds using the GNU-compatible `clang` frontend with MSVC runtime settings, generated runtime flags reflect MSVC dynamic runtime linkage when requested and avoid adding redundant runtime flags for static runtime mode.
For Windows builds using the GNU-compatible `clang` frontend with GNU-style toolchains, generated linker flags select the compatible LLVM linker frontend needed for MSVC-style linking.
The frontend-aware runtime and linker behavior is applied consistently in both `AutotoolsToolchain` and `GnuToolchain` outputs.
acceptance_criteria: When a Windows Conan configuration uses `compiler=clang` and the configured compiler executable is `clang-cl`, generated GNU-style toolchain flags should use the correct `clang-cl` C++ standard flag format.

When a Windows Conan configuration uses `compiler=clang`, the configured compiler executable is `clang`, and the MSVC runtime mode is dynamic, generated GNU-style toolchain flags should include the runtime-linkage information needed to link against the corresponding dynamic MSVC runtime library.

When a Windows Conan configuration uses `compiler=clang`, the configured compiler executable is `clang`, and the MSVC runtime mode is static, Conan should not add unnecessary explicit MSVC runtime flags that conflict with the frontend's default static behavior.
When GNU-style toolchains generate linker flags for Windows `clang` frontend builds using MSVC-style linking, the linker invocation should be directed to the compatible LLVM linker frontend.

When the same Windows LLVM/Clang configuration is used with either `AutotoolsToolchain` or `GnuToolchain`, the generated compile and link behavior should remain consistent with the selected frontend and runtime mode.
When the configuration does not match the affected Windows LLVM/Clang cases, Conan should preserve the existing flag-generation behavior.

task_21.title: Validate CycloneDX SBOM licenses against SPDX compatibility
task_21.description: The SBOM generator now distinguishes between SPDX-recognized licenses and custom or unknown license strings when producing CycloneDX output. Recognized licenses are emitted as identifiers, non-SPDX values are emitted as names, and each declared license in a multi-license package is classified independently. The update also adjusts CycloneDX 1.6 component author output to use structured author objects.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that generated CycloneDX SBOMs only encode licenses as SPDX identifiers when the declared license is SPDX-compatible, while preserving non-SPDX or custom licenses as names.
