Ensure that packages with multiple licenses keep one entry per declared license and that CycloneDX 1.6 component author information is emitted in structured author form.

expectation.grounded: When `conan.tools.sbom.cyclonedx_1_4()` or `conan.tools.sbom.cyclonedx_1_6()` serializes a recipe's `license` metadata into the SBOM `licenses` list, each value must be checked against the bundled SPDX license set using case-insensitive matching to decide whether it is treated as SPDX-compatible. SPDX-compatible values must be emitted under `license.id`; non-SPDX values must be emitted under `license.name`. This rule applies to both a single string license and iterable multi-license declarations, and each declared value must remain present as its own SBOM entry. In CycloneDX 1.6 component entries, author data must be represented through `authors` objects containing `name` values rather than a plain string `author` entry.
expectation.conceptual: SBOM generation should distinguish standard SPDX licenses from custom license labels instead of treating every license as an SPDX identifier. Known SPDX licenses should appear as license identifiers, unknown or project-specific licenses should appear as names, and mixed multi-license packages should classify each license independently. CycloneDX 1.6 author metadata should use the structured author format expected by downstream consumers.

constraints.grounded: Do not drop license metadata, merge multiple declared licenses into a single entry, or force custom licenses into the SPDX identifier field. Existing CycloneDX 1.4 and 1.6 SBOM generation behavior outside license field selection must remain intact, and CycloneDX 1.4 author handling should not be changed by this update.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should improve standards compliance without removing license information or requiring users to rename custom licenses. Packages with one, many, or mixed license declarations should continue to produce complete SBOM metadata.

behavior: CycloneDX SBOM generation validates declared license values against a bundled SPDX license list before choosing how to serialize them.
The SPDX compatibility check is case-insensitive when deciding whether a declared license should use the identifier field.
A SPDX-compatible declared license is emitted as `license.id`, while a non-SPDX or custom declared license is emitted as `license.name`.
When multiple licenses are declared, the generated SBOM contains one license entry per declared value and evaluates SPDX compatibility for each entry independently.
CycloneDX 1.6 component author metadata is emitted as structured `authors` entries with `name` fields instead of a bare string author value.
acceptance_criteria: When generating a CycloneDX 1.4 or 1.6 SBOM for a package with one SPDX-recognized license, the component should contain exactly one license entry using the SPDX identifier field for that value.

When generating a CycloneDX 1.4 or 1.6 SBOM for a package with one custom or unknown license string, the component should contain exactly one license entry using the license name field instead of the SPDX identifier field.

When generating a CycloneDX 1.4 or 1.6 SBOM for a package that declares multiple licenses, the SBOM should preserve the number of declared licenses and choose the identifier or name field independently for each one.

When generating a CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM for a component that has author metadata, the component should expose authors as structured author objects with `name` values rather than a plain string author field.

task_26.title: Honor excludes for symlinked directories in copy()
task_26.description: The 2.17.0 update fixes conan.tools.files.copy() so exclude patterns also suppress symlinks that point to folders. This brings symlinked directories in line with the existing exclusion behavior for regular folders and symlinked files, including the API's case-sensitive or case-insensitive matching mode.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan.tools.files.copy()` applies `excludes` patterns to symlinks that target directories, so excluded linked folders are not copied while other matching files and directories continue to be copied normally.

expectation.grounded: `conan.tools.files.copy()` must filter symlinked-folder matches through the `excludes` parameter the same way it already filters regular copied entries. When an excluded pattern matches a symlink that points to a folder, that symlink must be omitted from the copy operation. Matching for these symlinked folders must follow the existing `ignore_case` behavior: case-insensitive matching when enabled and case-sensitive matching otherwise.
expectation.conceptual: Directory symlinks should respect exclusion rules just like ordinary files, ordinary folders, and symlinked files. If a caller excludes a linked folder by name or pattern, the copy operation should leave it out, and exclusion matching should honor the API's configured case-sensitivity rules.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the meaning of `excludes` for non-symlink entries. Only symlinked folders whose relative names match an exclusion pattern should be suppressed, and non-excluded matches must remain eligible for copying under the existing pattern and case-matching rules.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be additive and targeted: excluded linked folders should stop being copied, while all previously valid non-excluded copy behavior should remain unchanged.

behavior: `conan.tools.files.copy()` now applies `excludes` filtering to the internal set of symlinked directories selected for copying.
A symlink that points to a folder is no longer copied when its relative path matches an `excludes` pattern.
Regular directories and files that match the copy pattern and are not excluded continue to be copied.
Exclusion checks for symlinked folders use case-insensitive matching when `ignore_case` is enabled.
Exclusion checks for symlinked folders use case-sensitive matching when `ignore_case` is disabled.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan.tools.files.copy()` is called with a source tree containing both a regular directory and a symlink to a directory, and `excludes` matches the symlink name, it should copy the regular directory but omit the symlinked directory from the destination.
When `excludes` does not match a symlinked directory selected by the copy pattern, that symlinked directory should remain eligible to be copied.
When `ignore_case` is enabled, an exclude pattern that differs only by letter case from a symlinked directory name should still prevent that symlink from being copied.
When `ignore_case` is disabled, a symlinked directory should only be excluded if its name matches the exclude pattern with exact case.

task_25.title: Handle grafted commits in Conan Git helper remote checks
task_25.description: Conan 2.17.0 fixes the Git helper so repositories checked out at grafted commits are no longer incorrectly treated as having a commit that is absent from the remote. This restores correct SCM coordinate discovery for APIs that validate the current revision against the remote before exporting repository metadata.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan's Git helper accepts grafted commits that are actually available from the configured remote, so SCM metadata generation does not incorrectly fail or skip repository coordinates for valid checkouts.

expectation.grounded: `Git.commit_in_remote()` should correctly report remote availability for a commit even when the local checkout is grafted, instead of rejecting it due to shallow-history assumptions. As a result, `Git.coordinates_to_conandata()` and `Git.get_url_and_commit()` should continue to produce the repository URL and commit metadata for valid grafted revisions that can be resolved from the remote.
expectation.conceptual: When a recipe runs from a repository checked out at a grafted commit, Conan should still recognize that revision as valid if the remote can provide it. Users should be able to export or inspect SCM coordinates from such repositories without the tooling behaving as though the commit is missing.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the existing safe-failure contract of `Git.commit_in_remote()`: if remote validation still cannot confirm the commit, it should continue to return a negative result rather than exposing fetch failures as a new outward exception path. Do not regress normal remote commit checks for non-grafted histories.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should broaden support for valid repository histories without changing how clearly unavailable commits are handled. Standard repositories must keep working as before, and invalid remote revisions must still fail safely.

behavior: `Git.commit_in_remote()` should no longer produce a false negative solely because the checked-out commit is grafted.
`Git.coordinates_to_conandata()` should include SCM repository data for a grafted current revision when that revision is present in the configured remote.
`Git.get_url_and_commit()` should return the current repository URL and commit for grafted revisions that remain fetchable from the remote.

If the remote cannot provide the requested commit for reasons unrelated to grafted history handling, the helper should continue reporting the commit as unavailable instead of surfacing a new user-visible exception.
acceptance_criteria: Given a repository checkout whose current revision is grafted but exists in the configured remote, when Conan evaluates SCM coordinates through the `Git` helper, it should treat that commit as present in the remote.

When `Git.coordinates_to_conandata()` is invoked for a repository at a valid grafted revision, it should produce repository coordinate metadata rather than behaving as though the commit is not in the remote.
When `Git.get_url_and_commit()` is invoked for a repository at a valid grafted revision, it should return the repository URL and current commit successfully.

When the requested commit genuinely cannot be validated against the remote, `Git.commit_in_remote()` should still fail safely with a negative result rather than changing to a new outward error behavior.

task_24.title: Deduplicate generated component dependencies in PkgConfigDeps and BazelDeps
task_24.description: Conan 2.17.0 fixes duplicated dependency entries emitted by PkgConfigDeps and BazelDeps when a component repeats the same requirement. Generated pkg-config and Bazel metadata should now contain each resolved component dependency name only once while preserving normal dependency naming and lookup behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Conan 2.17.0 stops PkgConfigDeps and BazelDeps from emitting duplicate dependency names when a package component declares the same requirement more than once.

expectation.grounded: When PkgConfigDeps or BazelDeps resolves component requirements from Conan component metadata, repeated references to the same package or component in cpp_info.requires must be collapsed so each resolved dependency name appears once in the generated output. Deduplication must apply after normal name resolution, including package-level references, component-level references, custom pkg_config_name mappings, and build-context suffixes used by PkgConfigDeps.
expectation.conceptual: Generated pkg-config and Bazel dependency metadata should treat repeated declarations of the same logical component dependency as a single dependency. Consumers should see one dependency entry per resolved dependency, even if the recipe declared that dependency multiple times.

constraints.grounded: Do not change how valid dependency names are resolved, how direct or transitive requirements are discovered, or how aliases and build-context naming are emitted; the intended behavioral change is removal of duplicate resolved dependency names from generated dependency lists.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should remove duplicates without altering normal dependency naming or causing dependencies to disappear. Existing generator behavior should remain the same aside from duplicate entries no longer being repeated.

behavior: PkgConfigDeps-generated .pc files list each resolved component requirement at most once in the Requires field, even if the same requirement is declared repeatedly.
BazelDeps-generated Bazel targets list each resolved component requirement at most once in deps, even if the same requirement is declared repeatedly.
Deduplication is based on the final exported dependency name, so renamed pkg-config dependencies and build-context-suffixed pkg-config dependencies are also emitted once.
Packages that do not contain duplicate component requirements continue to use the same dependency discovery flow and emit the same dependency set as before.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan component repeats the same component requirement multiple times, generating pkg-config metadata with PkgConfigDeps should produce a Requires list that contains that resolved dependency name only once.

When a Conan component repeats the same component requirement multiple times, generating Bazel metadata with BazelDeps should produce a deps list that contains that resolved dependency target only once.
When dependency names are customized through supported public naming properties or build-context suffixes, duplicate declarations should still collapse to a single emitted dependency name.
When component requirements are already unique, generation should continue to include all expected dependencies without introducing new omissions or renamed entries.

task_29.title: Allow mixed numeric conf values during composition
task_29.description: Conan 2.17.0 fixes configuration composition so numeric conf values can be combined even when different sources use different numeric categories, such as integers and floating-point numbers. This removes spurious composition failures while keeping normal configuration precedence and existing non-numeric compatibility rules unchanged.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that composing Conan conf values across profiles, scopes, or other merged configuration sources accepts values that are all numeric even when they use different numeric categories, instead of failing solely because one value is an integer and another is a floating-point number.

expectation.grounded: When `_ConfValue` instances are composed for the same conf entry, values whose runtime types are both subclasses of `numbers.Number` must be treated as compatible even if their concrete types differ. Composition of conf entries in `ConfDefinition` should therefore allow combinations such as `int` with `float` without raising the type-mismatch behavior previously triggered for differing types, while preserving normal conf precedence and lookup results.
expectation.conceptual: Configuration merging should accept mixed numeric values for the same setting. Users should be able to define a setting as one kind of number in one source and another kind of number in another source without the merge failing, and the usual override behavior should still decide which value is seen in each scope.

constraints.grounded: This compatibility relaxation applies only when both values are numeric. Existing handling for dictionaries, lists, and unset values must remain unchanged, and non-numeric type mismatches must continue to follow the prior compatibility rules.
constraints.conceptual: Only numeric-to-numeric combinations should gain the new flexibility. Other value categories should keep their current merge semantics, including existing protections against incompatible type combinations.

behavior: Composing the same conf key from multiple sources no longer fails when one value is an integer and the other is a floating-point number.
Mixed numeric categories are treated as compatible during conf composition, even when their concrete runtime types differ.
The fix affects runtime configuration merging behavior, including scoped or overridden conf values, without changing normal precedence resolution.
Existing merge behavior for collection values and unset values remains unchanged.
Existing rejection or special handling of incompatible non-numeric type combinations remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When two composed conf values for the same setting are both numeric but use different numeric categories, the configuration should compose successfully without a type-compatibility failure.

When a numeric conf value is defined in one source and a different numeric category is defined for the same setting in a more specific source, the resulting configuration should preserve normal override behavior rather than erroring during composition.
When composed conf values are non-numeric and incompatible, the library should continue to enforce its existing compatibility behavior.
When conf values are dictionaries, lists, or unset values, their pre-existing composition behavior should remain unchanged by this update.

task_27.title: Clarify filtered graph errors in conan list
task_27.description: The update improves the user-facing failure behavior of `conan list --graph=...` when the provided graph JSON is incomplete, especially when it was generated with filtering. Instead of surfacing an unclear internal failure caused by missing graph keys, the command should report that the graph file lacks required data and indicate that filtered graph files are not suitable input for the list command.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan list --graph=...` reports a clear, actionable error when the supplied graph JSON is missing required graph data, including the common case where the graph file was generated with graph filtering.

expectation.grounded: When `conan list` loads a graph file and required keys are absent from the JSON contents, the operation should raise a `ConanException` that identifies the graph file as missing required graph data and explains that filtered graph files are not valid input for the list command. Existing handling for invalid JSON input and unrelated exception paths should remain distinct.
expectation.conceptual: If a user passes an incomplete graph export to `conan list`, the command should fail with a helpful message that explains the input is missing required graph information and that filtered graph outputs cannot be reused for listing.

constraints.grounded: Do not change successful `conan list --graph=...` behavior for valid, complete graph files. Keep malformed JSON failures separated from missing-key graph-content failures, and preserve the command's existing error signaling through `ConanException`.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only improve diagnostics for incomplete graph inputs without changing normal list results or collapsing different input errors into the same generic failure.

behavior: The graph-loading path for `conan list --graph=...` now treats missing required JSON keys as a dedicated user-facing error condition.
When required graph content is absent, the command raises a `ConanException` instead of falling through to a less clear generic failure.
The reported error explains both that the graph file is incomplete and that filtered graph exports are not appropriate input for the list command.
Invalid JSON graph files continue to be reported as invalid JSON through a separate error path.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan list --graph=<file>` with a complete, supported graph JSON file, it should behave as before.
When a user runs `conan list --graph=<file>` with a graph JSON file that omits required graph keys, it should fail with a `ConanException` that clearly states the file is missing required graph data.
When the missing required graph data is due to a filtered graph export, the error should explicitly communicate that filtered graph files are not valid input for the list command.
When a user runs `conan list --graph=<file>` with malformed JSON, the command should continue to report an invalid JSON error rather than the missing-keys diagnostic.

task_28.title: Deterministic override serialization
task_28.description: Conan 2.17.0 makes serialized dependency override data stable by always emitting override entries in a consistent order. This prevents equivalent override configurations from producing different serialized outputs solely because the overrides were accumulated in a different order.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan serializes dependency override data deterministically so equivalent override configurations produce the same observable output regardless of accumulation order.

expectation.grounded: When Conan serializes overrides through `Overrides.serialize()`, each serialized override list for a given dependency must be emitted in a stable sorted order based on the serialized override references. Unset override entries must remain serializable and be placed deterministically alongside concrete override references.
expectation.conceptual: Serialized override metadata should be stable across runs: the same override content should always produce the same ordered output, including cases where some override entries are absent or unset.

constraints.grounded: Do not change which override groups are serialized or which override values are represented. Preserve support for null or unset override entries, and only normalize ordering within each serialized override list.
constraints.conceptual: The update should remove nondeterministic ordering without changing the meaning, membership, or validity of override data.

behavior: Conan now orders the serialized values within each override collection before producing serialized output.
The ordering is deterministic for concrete override references, so different accumulation orders no longer change the serialized representation.
Null or unset override entries continue to be included in serialized override data and are handled in a stable, predictable position.
acceptance_criteria: When the same set of overrides is serialized after being accumulated in different orders, the serialized override output should be identical.
When multiple concrete override references exist for the same serialized override group, they should appear in a consistent sorted order.
When an override group contains both concrete overrides and an unset override entry, serialization should succeed and produce a deterministic ordering.
When override content has not changed, upgrading should not add, remove, or reinterpret serialized override entries beyond normalizing their order.

task_31.title: Fix CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM authors field shape
task_31.description: The update corrects CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM output so author information is emitted in the schema-compliant structure expected by downstream consumers. This affects generated SBOM documents for both the main package metadata and listed components when author data is present.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM generation outputs author information in the correct schema-defined format for both the root component metadata and dependency components.

expectation.grounded: When `conan.tools.sbom.cyclonedx_1_6` generates an SBOM and `conanfile.author` or a dependency component author is defined, the resulting `metadata.component.authors` and `components[*].authors` entries must be arrays of author objects using the `name` field, rather than arrays of raw strings. If no author is defined, the `authors` field should remain absent.
expectation.conceptual: CycloneDX 1.6 SBOMs should represent authors in the format required by the specification so that author data is valid and interoperable wherever it appears in the document.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to the observable structure of the CycloneDX 1.6 `authors` field. Existing SBOM generation behavior for other fields, component inclusion, and documents without author data should not regress.
constraints.conceptual: Only the author representation should change; other SBOM content and cases without author information should continue to behave as before.

behavior: Generated CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM metadata uses an `authors` array of objects for the main component when the package declares an author.
Generated CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM component entries use an `authors` array of objects for dependency components when those components declare an author.
Each emitted author entry exposes the author name through the schema-defined `name` property instead of emitting the author as a plain string.
If a package or component does not define author information, the corresponding `authors` field is omitted.
acceptance_criteria: When a package with `author` metadata is exported to a CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM, the root component's `authors` field should contain object entries with a `name` value for each author.
When dependency components in a CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM include author metadata, each component's `authors` field should contain object entries with `name` values rather than plain strings.
When no author metadata is provided for the root package or a component, the generated CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM should omit that `authors` field.
The generated CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM should remain otherwise consistent apart from the corrected author-field structure.

task_32.title: Relocatable CMakeConfigDeps paths for deployers
task_32.description: The upgrade fixes `CMakeConfigDeps` so generated CMake references remain valid when dependencies are installed through deployers. Paths that previously resolved from absolute package locations are now emitted relative to the generated CMake files, improving relocatability without changing the intended dependency metadata.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `CMakeConfigDeps` produces relocatable generated CMake metadata for deployer-based installs, so consumers can resolve dependency package roots, include locations, runtime library directories, and declared CMake build modules from the deployed output instead of depending on original absolute package cache paths.

expectation.grounded: When the incubating `CMakeConfigDeps` generator is used together with deployers, generated CMake files should resolve dependency-related paths relative to `CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR`. This applies to dependency directory mappings for packages discovered through existing config files, aggregated runtime library directories exposed through generated path files, `cmake_build_modules` includes, package folder variables, and aggregated include directory variables. Public behavior should remain path-compatible for CMake consumers, with normalized forward-slash paths and unchanged dependency semantics apart from becoming relocatable.
expectation.conceptual: Using `CMakeConfigDeps` with a deployer should generate CMake metadata that keeps working after deployment because all consumer-visible dependency paths are expressed relative to the generated files. Projects should be able to find and use deployed dependencies, their runtime search paths, headers, and auxiliary CMake modules without relying on machine-specific absolute locations.

constraints.grounded: The change must preserve the existing dependency graph and exposed metadata meaning for `CMakeConfigDeps`; only the way paths are expressed should differ for deployer scenarios. Runtime directory aggregation must continue to avoid duplicate entries per configuration, and path normalization should remain compatible with CMake path syntax.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should improve relocatability without changing which dependencies, headers, runtime directories, or build modules are advertised. Consumers should observe the same dependency information as before, except that it remains valid from the deployed layout.

behavior: Generated dependency root references for packages resolved through existing CMake config files are emitted relative to the generated CMake file location instead of using absolute package folder paths.
Generated runtime library directory entries used by CMake path setup are converted to relative references anchored at the current generated file location.
Generated `cmake_build_modules` include references in package config output are converted from package-absolute paths to relative paths.
Generated package folder variables and aggregated include directory variables in target configuration output are rewritten as paths relative to the generated file location.
Generated paths continue to use CMake-compatible forward-slash formatting while preserving the same logical dependency contents.
acceptance_criteria: When `CMakeConfigDeps` is used with a deployer, the generated CMake files should reference deployed dependency locations through paths relative to the generated file directory rather than absolute cache paths.
When a dependency exposes CMake build modules, consuming the generated package config from the deployed output should still include those modules successfully after relocation.
When a consumer relies on generated package folder, include directory, or runtime library directory variables, those values should resolve correctly from the deployed layout.
When multiple runtime directories are aggregated for a configuration, the generated output should keep the existing set of unique directories while making them relocatable.

task_30.title: Fix python_requires test_package warning and create flow with tool_requires profiles
task_30.description: Conan 2.17.0 corrects `python_requires` test-package handling so deprecation warnings about `tested_reference_str` are only shown when the test package is actually missing that marker, and creating a `python_requires` package continues to work even when the selected profile declares `tool_requires`.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `python_requires` packages can be created and tested without spurious `tested_reference_str` deprecation warnings, and ensure that `conan create` for a `python_requires` package still succeeds when the active profile includes `tool_requires`.

expectation.grounded: When Conan loads a `test_package` for a `python_requires` package during `conan test` or `conan create`, it should recognize the `tested_reference_str` marker through the normal conanfile loading flow. If `test_package/conanfile.py` declares `python_requires = "tested_reference_str"`, Conan should bind the tested Python require without emitting a deprecation warning. If the marker is absent while a tested Python require is being injected, Conan should still proceed but emit a deprecation warning indicating that `tested_reference_str` should be declared. This behavior must also hold when `conan create` runs with profiles that include `tool_requires`.
expectation.conceptual: Testing or creating a Python-require package should only warn when the test package is actually using an outdated declaration pattern. Valid `tested_reference_str` usage should be accepted quietly, and adding tool requirements to the selected profile must not break package creation.

constraints.grounded: Do not emit the `tested_reference_str` deprecation warning for `test_package` conanfiles that already declare the marker. Preserve warning behavior for `test_package` conanfiles that receive a tested Python require but omit that declaration. Continue resolving the tested `python_requires` into the test package in both `conan test` and `conan create`, including executions that use profiles with `tool_requires`.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the warning narrow and accurate, preserve existing Python-require test-package resolution, and avoid introducing regressions in package creation when extra tool requirements are present in the profile.

behavior: When a `test_package` explicitly declares `python_requires` as `tested_reference_str`, Conan should treat that as the expected marker for the tested Python require and should not emit the related deprecation warning.

When a `test_package` is loaded with an injected tested Python require and does not declare `tested_reference_str`, Conan should still attach the tested Python require to the test package and emit a deprecation warning.

The warning decision for missing `tested_reference_str` should be made as part of conanfile loading for the `test_package`, so the same rule applies consistently across `conan test` and `conan create` flows.
Running `conan create` for a `python_requires` package with a profile that contains `tool_requires` should complete without breaking the test-package flow for the tested Python require.
acceptance_criteria: Given a `python_requires` package whose `test_package` declares `python_requires` as `tested_reference_str`, when the package is created or its test package is run, then Conan should execute the test package without emitting the `tested_reference_str` deprecation warning.

Given a `python_requires` package whose `test_package` does not declare `tested_reference_str`, when Conan injects the tested Python require for the test package, then Conan should continue execution and emit a deprecation warning about the missing marker.

Given a `python_requires` package and a profile that declares one or more `tool_requires`, when `conan create` is executed with that profile, then the create flow should still complete the test-package stage successfully.
When the same `python_requires` test package is executed through either `conan test` or `conan create`, Conan should apply the same warning behavior for `tested_reference_str` in both entry points.

task_33.title: Bundle Full Conan Package in PyInstaller Builds
task_33.description: PyInstaller-based Conan distributions should package the full runtime Conan module set instead of a manually enumerated subset so frozen executables do not fail when commands or recipes import shipped Conan submodules that were previously omitted. Test-only Conan modules should remain excluded from the bundle.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan builds produced with PyInstaller include the complete runtime Conan package so packaged executables can load shipped Conan commands and tool modules without missing-module failures, while excluding test-only content from the bundle.

expectation.grounded: When generating a PyInstaller bundle for Conan, the bundle should collect submodules across the `conan` package rather than relying on a fixed list of hidden imports for selected `conan.tools` and command modules. The packaged application should continue to include the required non-Conan support imports already needed for the frozen runtime, and it should exclude `conan.test.*` from the collected Conan modules.
expectation.conceptual: A frozen Conan executable should behave like a normal Conan installation with respect to loading built-in Conan modules. Users should be able to invoke bundled commands and recipe/tooling functionality without runtime import errors caused by incomplete packaging, while test-only code remains absent from the shipped artifact.

constraints.grounded: Do not narrow the PyInstaller bundle back to a hand-curated subset of Conan modules. Preserve the existing frozen-runtime support imports needed outside the Conan package, and avoid bundling Conan test namespaces.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should expand runtime module availability without introducing test content into the distributable or regressing existing frozen-build compatibility behavior.

behavior: PyInstaller packaging for Conan now includes the full set of importable `conan` submodules instead of enumerating only specific command and `conan.tools` modules.
Frozen Conan executables should no longer depend on a manually maintained allowlist to access built-in Conan modules at runtime.
Modules under `conan.test.*` are excluded from the packaged Conan module collection.
Previously required non-Conan hidden imports used by the frozen runtime remain part of the PyInstaller build inputs.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan is bundled with PyInstaller, invoking packaged Conan functionality that imports shipped `conan` submodules should not fail solely because those modules were omitted from the bundle.
When the PyInstaller bundle is produced, it should contain runtime Conan submodules broadly across the `conan` package rather than only a predefined subset of tools and commands.
When reviewing the bundled Conan module scope, test-only namespaces under `conan.test` should not be included.
When building the frozen Conan distribution on supported platforms, the bundle should retain the pre-existing auxiliary imports needed for correct runtime behavior outside the Conan package.

task_34.title: Remove libtool setup from autotools executable template
task_34.description: The 2.17.0 update fixes the `conan new autotools_exe` template so it generates an executable-oriented Autotools configuration instead of reusing a library-oriented one that initializes libtool unnecessarily. This avoids introducing libtool-specific setup into newly generated executable projects while preserving the normal Autotools configuration needed to build them.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan new autotools_exe` creates executable-only Autotools projects without enabling libtool, so newly generated templates do not impose unnecessary libtool-related configuration on users building executables.

expectation.grounded: The `conan new autotools_exe` template should generate a `configure.ac` for executable packages that does not include `LT_INIT`. The generated template should continue to initialize the standard Autotools checks required for C++ compilation and archive tool support, and it should still configure the expected Makefiles for the executable project layout.
expectation.conceptual: Creating a new Autotools executable project should produce a configuration suitable for a plain executable build, without adding library-tooling setup that the project does not need. The generated project should remain ready for normal Autotools configure and build flows for executables.

constraints.grounded: The change should be limited to the executable template generated by `conan new autotools_exe`. It must not reintroduce libtool initialization through shared library-oriented template content, and it must preserve the generated project's ability to detect the C++ compiler, archiver support, and produce the configured build files used by the template.
constraints.conceptual: Only the unnecessary library-specific behavior should be removed. The executable template should keep the existing build setup needed to configure and build successfully, without expanding scope into unrelated template behavior changes.

behavior: Running `conan new autotools_exe` now generates an Autotools configuration for executables that omits libtool initialization.
The executable template no longer inherits library-specific `configure.ac` behavior that would otherwise enable libtool for a non-library project.
The generated executable project still includes the standard Autotools tool discovery and build-file generation needed for a C++ executable template.
acceptance_criteria: Given a project created with `conan new autotools_exe`, when its generated Autotools configuration is inspected, it should not contain `LT_INIT` or any equivalent libtool initialization.
When a user bootstraps and configures a freshly generated Autotools executable project, the workflow should not depend on libtool-specific setup that is only relevant to library builds.

When `conan new autotools_exe` generates a project, it should still provide the expected Autotools configuration necessary to detect the C++ toolchain and configure the project's build files for the executable template.

task_36.title: Prevent conan audit threshold crashes on unscanned packages
task_36.description: Conan 2.17.0 fixes a crash in `conan audit` when severity-threshold evaluation encounters package entries that were not found or not scanned and therefore have no vulnerability payload. The command should skip those entries and continue evaluating actual vulnerability data instead of failing during audit result parsing.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan audit` does not crash while applying an error threshold when the audit response includes packages that were not scanned or not found and therefore do not provide vulnerability information.

expectation.grounded: When `conan audit` evaluates a scan result against a severity threshold, `_parse_error_threshold` should ignore package entries that do not include a `vulnerabilities` section, including entries that only report a package-level error because the package was not found in the catalog. Entries that do include vulnerability edges must still be checked against the configured threshold, and qualifying scores must continue to trigger the normal `conan_error` failure signal.
expectation.conceptual: Threshold-based audit evaluation should consider only packages with vulnerability data. Packages that could not be scanned should not crash the audit command, and real threshold violations from successfully scanned packages should still be reported normally.

constraints.grounded: Do not treat package entries without vulnerability data as threshold violations, and do not suppress threshold failures for other package references in the same audit result. Existing threshold behavior for vulnerability entries with qualifying CVSS scores must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: Ignore incomplete audit entries for threshold comparison, but preserve the existing failure behavior for actual vulnerabilities that meet the configured severity threshold.

behavior: `conan audit` skips audit result entries that lack vulnerability data when evaluating a severity threshold.
A package entry reported as not found or otherwise unscanned no longer causes threshold parsing to fail.
Other packages in the same audit result that contain vulnerability edges are still compared against the configured CVSS threshold.
If a scanned package meets or exceeds the threshold, the audit still emits its normal threshold failure signal.
acceptance_criteria: When an audit result contains a package entry with only an error and no vulnerability section, running `conan audit` with a severity threshold should complete without crashing on that entry.
When a package is not found in the catalog and therefore has no vulnerability data, that package should be ignored for threshold comparison rather than treated as a threshold failure.
When another package in the same audit result includes a preferred CVSS base score at or above the configured threshold, `conan audit` should still fail with its normal threshold error behavior.
When audit results contain a mix of scanned and unscanned packages, threshold evaluation should continue to operate on the scanned packages only.

task_35.title: Fix CMakeConfigDeps conditional link flags
task_35.description: Conan 2.17.0 fixes CMakeConfigDeps so exported link flags for shared libraries, module libraries, and executables are emitted as proper conditional CMake link options. This restores correct propagation of package-defined link flags to compatible consumer target types.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeConfigDeps-generated package targets propagate exported link flags correctly so shared-library and module-library flags apply only to compatible library consumers, executable flags apply only to executable consumers, and consumer builds do not lose or mis-handle those link options.

expectation.grounded: CMakeConfigDeps must expose package `sharedlinkflags` and `exelinkflags` through generated target `INTERFACE_LINK_OPTIONS` using active CMake generator expressions rather than quoted string literals. `sharedlinkflags` must be evaluated only for consumer targets whose CMake `TYPE` is `SHARED_LIBRARY` or `MODULE_LIBRARY`, and `exelinkflags` must be evaluated only for consumer targets whose `TYPE` is `EXECUTABLE`.
expectation.conceptual: Packages that publish CMake link flags should have those flags reach consumers in a form CMake interprets correctly. Conditional link flags must be honored for the right consumer target kinds, without being suppressed or malformed by how they are emitted.

constraints.grounded: Do not expand the scope of these link flags beyond the existing target-type conditions. Non-matching consumer target types must not receive the corresponding `sharedlinkflags` or `exelinkflags`, and unrelated CMakeConfigDeps-generated metadata must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: Limit the change to correcting conditional link-option propagation. The fix must not alter which kinds of consumers are eligible for those flags or change unrelated package metadata.

behavior: Generated CMakeConfigDeps targets now append `sharedlinkflags` to `INTERFACE_LINK_OPTIONS` as unquoted generator expressions that activate for `SHARED_LIBRARY` consumers.
Generated CMakeConfigDeps targets now append `sharedlinkflags` to `INTERFACE_LINK_OPTIONS` as unquoted generator expressions that activate for `MODULE_LIBRARY` consumers.
Generated CMakeConfigDeps targets now append `exelinkflags` to `INTERFACE_LINK_OPTIONS` as unquoted generator expressions that activate for `EXECUTABLE` consumers.
Matching consumers receive exported link flags as actual CMake link options instead of quoted conditional expressions that can interfere with correct interpretation.
acceptance_criteria: When a package defines `sharedlinkflags` and a consumer links it into a shared library through CMakeConfigDeps, the consumer should receive those link options during linking.
When a package defines `sharedlinkflags` and a consumer links it into a module library through CMakeConfigDeps, the consumer should receive those link options during linking.
When a package defines `exelinkflags` and a consumer links it into an executable through CMakeConfigDeps, the consumer should receive those link options during linking.
When the consumer target type does not match the exported flag category, those link options should not be applied.
When exported link flags contain multiple options, consumers should receive them as usable link options rather than as a single quoted conditional expression.

task_37.title: Fix missing require details for the first HTML graph edge
task_37.description: The 2.17.0 update fixes a user-visible bug in the HTML output of `conan graph info` where the first dependency edge could fail to display its require information when selected. The generated HTML graph should now treat the first selectable graph element as a valid selection and show its associated dependency details consistently.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the HTML output from `conan graph info -f=html` displays require information when the first dependency edge in the graph is selected, instead of behaving as if nothing was selected.

expectation.grounded: In the HTML produced by `conan graph info -f=html`, selecting an edge whose position resolves to the first graph entry must be handled as a valid selection. The details pane should populate from the selected node or edge data, and for the first dependency edge it should show the corresponding require information rather than omitting it.
expectation.conceptual: Users viewing the HTML dependency graph should be able to click the first dependency relationship and see the same dependency details they would expect from any other edge, including its require information.

constraints.grounded: The formatter must distinguish between an unselected graph element and a selected element whose identifier is the first valid entry. Existing detail rendering for other nodes and edges in `conan graph info -f=html` should remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should only correct the missing-details case for the first selectable graph element and must not regress normal graph inspection for the rest of the HTML view.

behavior: The generated HTML graph now recognizes the first selectable item in the graph as a real selection instead of treating it as absent.
When the first dependency edge is selected in the HTML graph, its require information is shown in the details area.
Selection-driven detail rendering continues to work for other nodes and edges without changing their expected behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan graph info -f=html` and opens the generated HTML graph, selecting the first dependency edge should display its require information.
When the selected graph element is the first valid node or edge in the HTML graph, the details panel should populate instead of remaining empty.
When users select non-first nodes or edges in the HTML graph, their detail display should continue to behave as before.

task_38.title: Refine cache save archives and add source exclusion
task_38.description: Conan 2.17.0 changes `conan cache save` so saved cache archives contain reusable recipe and package state instead of bundling transient downloaded artifacts. It also adds a `--no-source` option so users can omit recipe source folders from the exported cache snapshot when they want a smaller or source-free backup.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan cache save` creates clean, restorable cache snapshots without re-bundling transient downloaded artifact archives, and allow users to exclude recipe source folders from the saved `.tgz` by using `--no-source`.

expectation.grounded: The `conan cache save` command, and the corresponding cache save API behavior, should archive recipe export content, exported sources, recipe source folders by default, package folders, and restore-related metadata, while excluding downloaded artifact caches such as `conan_export.tgz`, `conan_sources.tgz`, downloaded package archives, and other transient cache-only directories. When `--no-source` is supplied, the saved archive should omit recipe source folders but still preserve the remaining selected recipe, package, and metadata content needed for restore.
expectation.conceptual: Saving the Conan cache should produce a focused backup of reusable recipe and package state rather than a recursive copy of every cache subfolder. By default, local recipe sources remain included, and users can explicitly opt out of saving those sources with `--no-source` without losing the rest of the restorable cache contents.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress restore support for saved recipe exports, exported sources, package contents, or associated metadata. Excluding downloaded artifacts must not prevent restoring the selected references, and `--no-source` must affect only recipe source folders rather than exported recipe data, package payloads, or metadata.
constraints.conceptual: The new archive filtering must reduce unwanted transient content without breaking normal cache backup and restore flows. Excluding sources must be a narrow opt-out that removes only recipe source material and leaves the rest of the saved cache usable.

behavior: `conan cache save` now saves recipe entries from selected reusable recipe content and metadata instead of recursively zipping the entire recipe cache directory.
Downloaded recipe-side archives such as `conan_export.tgz` and `conan_sources.tgz` are excluded from the saved cache bundle.
Saved package entries include the package payload and package metadata, but exclude transient package-side cache content such as downloaded package archives and build directories.
Using `conan cache save ... --no-source` omits recipe source folders from the exported cache archive.
Restoring a cache archive created by this flow recreates only the recipe/package state that was intentionally saved, and does not reintroduce excluded transient artifact caches.
acceptance_criteria: When a cache contains downloaded recipe archive files and the user runs `conan cache save`, the generated archive should not preserve those downloaded artifact files for a later restore.
When a cache contains package binaries and related metadata, saving and restoring the cache should recreate the package payload and metadata needed for normal reuse.
When a cache contains transient build output or downloaded package archive caches, saving and restoring the cache should not recreate those transient directories or files.
When the user runs `conan cache save ... --no-source`, restoring the saved archive should not recreate recipe source folder contents.
When the user runs `conan cache save` without `--no-source`, existing recipe source folder contents should remain included in the saved and restored cache snapshot.

task_39.title: Support creating python-requires packages with profile tool_requires
task_39.description: Conan 2.17.0 fixes a create-time failure for recipes intended to be consumed through python_requires. Running `conan create` for those packages should succeed even when the selected profile defines `tool_requires`, because Conan now avoids building an unnecessary dependency graph for a python-requires-only root recipe.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan create` can create a package meant to be used as `python_requires` even when the active profile contains `tool_requires`, without failing due to unrelated dependency graph resolution.

expectation.grounded: When `conan create` is executed for a recipe that is being created as a `python_requires` package and that root recipe does not declare regular `requires` or direct `tool_requires`, Conan should not attempt to resolve a full dependency graph just because the selected profile contains `tool_requires`. In that case, the create flow should proceed with a root-only graph and complete successfully. Recipes that actually declare dependencies should continue to use the normal graph-building path.
expectation.conceptual: Creating a helper package for reuse through `python_requires` should work under the same profiles used elsewhere in the workspace, including profiles that add tool dependencies. The command should only resolve dependency information that is relevant to that package instead of failing on an unnecessary graph calculation.

constraints.grounded: Keep existing dependency resolution behavior unchanged for recipes that declare actual `requires` or `tool_requires`. The special-case handling should apply only when the create flow is for a `python_requires` root recipe with no graph dependencies of its own.
constraints.conceptual: Limit the fix to the failing edge case. Normal package creation and dependency handling should behave the same for recipes with real dependencies.

behavior: A `python_requires` package can be created with `conan create` even if the chosen profile defines `tool_requires`.

For a `python_requires` root recipe with no declared regular or direct tool requirements, Conan skips full dependency graph construction and treats the package as a standalone root for the create flow.
Recipes that do declare regular dependencies or direct tool requirements still go through normal dependency graph resolution.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe is created for use as `python_requires` and the active profile contains one or more `tool_requires`, `conan create` should not fail solely because of those profile tool requirements.
When that `python_requires` recipe has no declared regular dependencies and no direct tool requirements, the create flow should complete without requiring a full dependency graph to be resolved.
When a recipe declares actual regular dependencies or direct tool requirements, `conan create` should continue to resolve them through the standard dependency graph behavior.

task_40.title: Honor parent .conanignore files during config install
task_40.description: Conan 2.17.0 fixes `conan config install` so ignore rules can be discovered from a `.conanignore` located above the selected source folder inside the installed configuration tree. This prevents unintended files from being copied when installing a nested configuration subset while keeping the ignore lookup bounded to the requested install root.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan config install` applies `.conanignore` rules when installing a nested configuration folder, including cases where the relevant `.conanignore` is stored in an ancestor directory of the selected source folder within the configuration being installed, so unrelated files are not copied into the Conan cache.

expectation.grounded: `conan config install` should search upward from the effective source folder for a `.conanignore` file and apply its ignore and include patterns during folder installation. The search should stop at the original install root, and installation should proceed normally when no `.conanignore` is found in that bounded path.
expectation.conceptual: Installing configuration content from a subdirectory should still honor the repository's intended ignore rules if they are defined higher in that configuration tree. Only ignore rules that belong to the configuration being installed should affect the result.

constraints.grounded: The change must preserve existing `conan config install` behavior when no `.conanignore` is present, continue treating `.conanignore` itself as excluded content, and avoid applying ignore files found above the requested configuration root.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be additive and safe: existing installs without ignore files should behave the same, the ignore file should not be copied as payload, and outside directories must not unexpectedly influence the install.

behavior: `conan config install` now resolves `.conanignore` by walking upward from the selected source folder instead of only checking that exact folder.
Ignore and re-include rules from the discovered `.conanignore` affect which files and directories are copied during configuration folder installation.
If no `.conanignore` exists between the selected source folder and the install root, installation copies files without additional ignore rules beyond the default exclusions.
The upward lookup is bounded to the install root, so ignore files outside the requested configuration tree do not alter the installation outcome.
acceptance_criteria: When `conan config install` installs configuration content from a nested source folder and an ancestor directory within that installed configuration contains a `.conanignore`, it should apply that file's ignore rules to the copied result.
When a parent `.conanignore` excludes files under the selected nested source folder, those excluded files should not be installed into the Conan cache.
When no `.conanignore` exists in the selected source folder or any of its ancestors up to the install root, the nested configuration files should still be installed normally.
When a `.conanignore` exists only outside the requested configuration root, running `conan config install` should ignore it and leave the installation result unaffected by that external file.
